comparedAgainst: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/graph-and-its-representations/ -- ad-dense reference page with static, non-themed raster diagrams (no dark mode, not tuned for a 390px viewport) and no measured memory numbers anywhere; this article's single theme-aware SVG showing the same graph as matrix + list + edge list side by side, plus a real GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread measurement table, is a clear step up.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adjacency_list -- covers matrix vs. list in prose with one generic, unthemed diagram and no worked C# code, no crossover measurement, no exercises; this article's stacked three-way figure and two collapsible exercises (find-the-bug, predict-the-crossover) teach the mechanism Wikipedia only states.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.dictionary-2 -- reference API docs: functional and responsive but no diagrams, no comparative trade-off table, no worked measurement; this article's Figure 1 and its 'What each operation costs' table build the comparison MS Learn doesn't attempt.
justification: Real numbers from a serial `verify-page.mjs --drafts` run in the worktree: Lighthouse 100/100/100/100, zero console errors (report.json consoleErrors: []), zero broken links (broken: []), mobileOverflowPx 0, h1 count 1, zero placeholder/NEEDS_MARKUS markers, words=2820, fig=1. The lighthouse-full.json failing sub-audits (max-potential-fid 330ms, bf-cache prevented, network-dependency-tree) are shared page-shell/script behavior, not this article's markup, and do not move the four category scores below the round's 90 floor. Structure follows shape C sensibly across seven sections: an untitled vocabulary lede (graph/vertex/edge, directed/undirected/weighted), 'The same graph, stored three ways' (the required figure plus a cross-checking C# program), 'What each operation costs' (the O-notation trade-off table), 'Weighted and directed variants' (a second worked program plus the find-the-bug exercise), 'Measuring memory instead of counting Big-O terms' (the crossover measurement plus a :::pitfall), 'When there's no graph to store: implicit graphs' (a third worked program), and 'Choosing a representation' (a bulleted decision guide plus the predict-the-crossover exercise) -- each section builds on the last and the shape never repeats the same rhythm twice in a row. The required diagram (Figure 1, viewBox 360x590) was inspected directly in mobile-light-part02/mobile-dark-part02 and desktop-light-part02 (390 CSS px and full-width renders): the graph, the 5x5 matrix, the five adjacency-list rows and the one edge-list row are all legible with generous, consistent spacing top to bottom -- no cramping or overlap anywhere in the 590-unit height, margins between the three labeled sub-sections (18-22 viewBox units) are even, and roughly 22 units of clean bottom padding follow the edge-list box. Colors (d-box-accent circles, d-text-accent matrix marks, d-line paths) are correctly theme-aware in both screenshots -- teal accent in light, the same hue lightened for contrast in dark, no literal fill/stroke colors bleeding through. The figure's source markup (lines 50-116 of the article) has no blank line between ``, avoiding the known Markdown-mangling issue. The figcaption ('the matrix marks every edge twice... the edge list is the shortest of the three') states a real, non-decorative takeaway the drawing actually shows (relative size/shape of the three representations), and the figure earns its place: the prose right after it explains AddEdge/Neighbors asymmetry in terms a reader who just looked at the three drawn shapes can follow directly. All eleven code fences use correct language tags matching tools/run-code.mjs conventions (`csharp run id=...` paired 1:1 with a directly-following `text output` block, matching the exercise and solution csharp run blocks too) and render with the site's standard C#-label/Copy-button/dark-output-panel treatment in both themes; the 'V = 1,000...' memory table inside the text output block is narrowed to fit within roughly 40 columns and is fully visible on mobile with no scroll (confirmed in mobile-light-part09), consistent with WRITER_GUIDE.md's phone-width output-panel rule. Both exercises are well-formed per WRITER_GUIDE.md: 'Find the bug in a one-way matrix' (mobile-light-part08) shows only the buggy program and the question, with the fix and its verifying re-run correctly hidden behind the collapsed 'Show solution' toggle; 'Predict the next crossover' (mobile-light-part12) is a genuine predict-then-reason exercise with no output panel shown before the question, and its solution is likewise collapsed. Neither exercise leaks its answer above the fold. The one real article-level nit: the 'What each operation costs' table has four columns (Operation, Adjacency matrix, Adjacency list, Edge list), one more than WRITER_GUIDE.md section 7's 'prefer at most three columns' guidance for phones. Confirmed in mobile-light-part04 and mobile-dark-part04: at 390px only the Operation column and part of the Adjacency matrix column are visible (the 'Add a vertex' row's 'O(V²) (rebuild the matrix)' cell and even the column header 'Adjacency matrix' itself are cut mid-word), with the Adjacency list and Edge list columns entirely off-screen behind the shared fade cue. This is a real instance of the exact failure mode the guide warns about ('four columns... will put half the table off-screen'), though it is a minor, not major, defect here: every cell value is short (mostly bare O(...) notation), nothing the prose depends on is stated only in a hidden cell (unlike a prior pillar sibling's near-identical table issue where a whole recommendation sentence lived only in the clipped column), and a reader who scrolls right gets clean, unbroken comparisons column by column rather than a jumbled reveal. It costs the reader three extra swipes to compare all three representations at a glance, which is a real friction point for a table whose whole job is a side-by-side trade-off comparison, but it does not hide any information permanently.

issues.location: 'What each operation costs' table (mobile-light-part04 / mobile-dark-part04 of `.verify/data-structures__graphs-representation/`)
issues.problem: The table has four columns (Operation, Adjacency matrix, Adjacency list, Edge list); WRITER_GUIDE.md section 7 recommends at most three on a phone. At 390px only Operation and part of Adjacency matrix are visible -- the header word 'matrix' and the 'Add a vertex' row's '(rebuild the matrix)' annotation are cut mid-word -- and the Adjacency list and Edge list columns are entirely off-screen, reachable only by scrolling past the fade cue. No content is permanently hidden (everything is reachable by scrolling, and cell values are short O(...) terms), but a reader cannot compare all three representations for one operation without three separate horizontal scrolls, which undercuts the table's purpose as the article's central trade-off comparison.
issues.fixLooksLike: Either shorten the parenthetical annotations (e.g. 'O(1)' / 'O(V²) rebuild' instead of 'O(V²) (rebuild the matrix)') so more of column 2 fits before the fade, or split the table into two narrower tables (e.g. 'lookup and mutation costs' and 'bulk-traversal and space costs') so each stays closer to three columns, or reformat as a short per-representation list under each of the three names. Any of these keeps all six operations comparable within one or two swipes instead of three.
